question.text: A NIFTY 25,000 put option is trading at a premium of Rs 250 when NIFTY spot is at 25,100. Using only the moneyness, intrinsic value, and delta-range facts in the NISM Series IV (pp.134, 137) and Series VIII (p.77) workbooks, which of the following statements is correct?

answer.text: The put is out-of-the-money (since spot 25,100 > strike 25,000), it has zero intrinsic value (Rs 250 premium is entirely time value), and its long-put delta lies somewhere strictly between 0 and -0.50
The put is in-the-money with intrinsic value of Rs 100, and its delta is approximately -0.80
The put has positive (call-like) delta because the premium of Rs 250 exceeds the spot-strike gap of Rs 100
The put is at-the-money with delta exactly -1.00

explanation.text: The Logic: A put is in-the-money when spot < strike. Here spot 25,100 > strike 25,000, so the put is out-of-the-money. NISM Series IV (pp.134, 137) and Series VIII (p.77) define intrinsic value of a put as max(Strike - Spot, 0) = max(25,000 - 25,100, 0) = 0, so the entire Rs 250 premium is time value. The same workbook material states long-put delta lies between 0 and -1, and for an OTM put is strictly between 0 and -0.50. The keyed statement combines all three workbook-supported facts. The Trap: The "ITM with Rs 100 intrinsic value" option inverts the moneyness rule for puts. A "positive delta" put is impossible - long puts always have non-positive delta. "ATM with delta exactly -1" contradicts both the moneyness check and the workbook delta range. The audit flagged the original because the keyed numeric range of "-0.40 to -0.45" cannot be derived from moneyness and premium alone without expiry, volatility, rates, and model assumptions. Note: The original asked for a specific numerical delta estimate (-0.40 to -0.45), which the workbook does not provide without additional model inputs (expiry, volatility, rates). The item has been rewritten to test the workbook-supported facts - moneyness, intrinsic value, and the long-put delta range - which uniquely identify the keyed statement (NISM Series IV pp.134, 137; Series VIII p.77).
